transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I keep losing chunks of time lately. I find myself re-reading emails and texts over and over, or reopening folders on my computer. And before I leave the house or start my work, I end up... mentally replaying conversations. It's like I’m just trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some kind of serious mistake. It's really starting to interfere with my day.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that keep popping into your mind and are difficult to get rid of?

Yes, I do. It happens a lot. Even when I’m right in the middle of something requiring my full attention, like trying to work through a system design for my job or prepare a lesson, this thought just keeps barging in. 

I'll suddenly start worrying that I might have sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I somehow mishandled some family photos, or maybe let someone in the community down. It's incredibly frustrating because I just can’t seem to let the thought pass... even though I know logically that I’ve already been over it. It just sticks there.
Do you feel compelled to repeat certain actions over and over?

Yeah, that's exactly what I meant earlier when I was talking about losing time. I feel like I have to keep going back and checking things. I'll read the same email or text message over and over again, or I'll just keep reopening the same folders on my computer. And it's not just physical things—before I can even leave the house or sit down to start my work, I feel forced to mentally replay conversations in my head. It's like I have to do these things repeatedly just to prove to myself that I didn't mess up or make a serious mistake.
Do you feel anxious when these thoughts or compulsions occur?

Yes, absolutely. It's a very strong sense of anxiety. When the thought pops into my head that I might have messed something up, my chest gets tight and I just feel this overwhelming worry. And the anxiety doesn't really go away until I go back and check the emails or replay the conversation in my head. But even then, the relief doesn't last very long before the anxiety starts creeping back in.
Do you ever have disturbing or intrusive thoughts that aren't related to something you feel compelled to do?

No, I don't think so. Pretty much every time I get one of those thoughts, it comes with that urge to... to go check or fix it. I haven't really noticed having any disturbing thoughts that just happen without me feeling like I need to do something about them. It's always tied to a mistake I think I made, and then I have to go verify it.
Are you trying to prevent something bad from happening when you repeat these actions or mentally replay conversations?

Yes, pretty much. It's... well, like I was saying earlier, that's the whole reason I keep losing those big chunks of time. Whether I'm re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders on my computer, or mentally replaying conversations before I can even leave the house or start my work... it really just comes down to trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake. I just have to be absolutely sure I didn't do something wrong that's going to cause a disaster.
Have you ever had thoughts that kept repeating in your mind and caused you distress, but you didn't feel like you had to do anything about them?

No, I don't think I have. Like I mentioned just a minute ago, it seems like every time I get stuck on one of those thoughts, it always comes with that strong urge to go check on it. I haven't really experienced having a distressing thought just repeating on its own without me feeling that need to take action or figure it out. It's always tied to needing to prove I didn't mess up.
Are these thoughts and compulsions to repeat actions affecting your relationships or work performance?

Yes, they definitely are. It's... well, my work has really slowed down because of all this checking. I've actually missed a few design milestones recently, which isn't like me. And I've had to postpone mentoring sessions with junior staff that I used to handle pretty reliably. 

It's affecting things outside of work, too. I volunteer for a youth coding workshop—it's something that really matters to me—and I felt incredibly embarrassed recently because I showed up late and completely unprepared because I got stuck in one of those loops before I left the house. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way.
Are your repetitive actions or mental replays specifically intended to prevent something bad or harmful from happening?

I think we just covered that, actually. Like I said a minute ago, yes, it's all about trying to prove to myself that I didn't make a mistake that's going to cause some kind of disaster. That's the whole reason I do the checking and the replaying.
How would you rate the level of distress these thoughts and compulsions are causing you?

I'd say it's... well, it's pretty moderate. It's not like I'm completely paralyzed by it every single minute of the day, but it's definitely there, and it's definitely a problem. It's enough to throw off my schedule and make me feel pretty anxious and frustrated a lot of the time.
Have you noticed any significant problems in your personal relationships due to these thoughts and compulsions?

No, not really. I mean, my wife has noticed that I'm a bit more stressed lately, and maybe taking longer to get ready to leave the house, but we haven't had any big arguments about it or anything. My friendships seem fine, too. It's mostly just impacting my work and my schedule, like I mentioned, rather than causing actual problems with the people in my life.
Have you had to take time off work or significantly reduce your work or social activities because of these thoughts and compulsions?

Well, I haven't had to take actual time off, but it's definitely slowing me down. At work, I've missed a few design milestones recently because I get so caught up in checking things. And... I've had to postpone some mentoring sessions that I usually handle without any issue. It's affecting my outside activities a bit, too. I volunteer at a youth coding workshop, and the other day I showed up late and completely unprepared because I was stuck in one of my loops before leaving the house. It was pretty embarrassing, honestly. So, yeah, it's definitely getting in the way.
Do you have any compulsions to perform specific physical actions, like handwashing or checking locks?

No, not physical things like washing my hands or checking the door locks. It's more... well, it's mostly digital and mental. I keep losing big chunks of time just re-reading emails and texts over and over. Or I'll keep reopening folders on my computer. And I also get stuck mentally replaying conversations before I can leave the house or start working. It's like... I'm just trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. That's really the main reason I came in to see you.
Do you feel like these repetitive thoughts and actions are in line with your own values and desires, or do they feel alien or contrary to who you are?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't really thought about it in terms of my values. I mean... I definitely don't want to be doing these things. I'd much rather just do my job and go about my day without all the delays. 

But I don't know if I'd say they feel alien, exactly. It's just my own brain getting stuck, I guess. It's just me trying to make sure I didn't make a mistake somewhere. It doesn't feel like someone else is putting the thoughts there, it just feels like a really frustrating cycle that I can't seem to break out of.
Have you noticed any changes in your overall quality of life since these symptoms started?

Yeah, I have. It really goes back to what I was saying earlier. The fact that my work has slowed down so much that I'm missing those design milestones... that's tough for me. I've always prided myself on being reliable, so having to postpone the mentoring sessions I used to handle without a problem is really frustrating. 

And like I mentioned with that youth coding workshop—that program really matters to me. So showing up late and completely unprepared, and dealing with that embarrassment... it just makes me feel like I'm letting people down across the board. So, yes, my day-to-day quality of life has definitely taken a hit because of all this.
Are there any activities or situations that you're avoiding because of these thoughts or compulsions?

I don't think I'm really avoiding anything, no. I mean, I still try to do everything I normally would—like my job, the mentoring, the workshops. The problem isn't that I'm staying away from certain situations, it's just that it takes me so much longer to actually get to them or get them done because I get stuck in those loops of checking and replaying things. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything specific.
